title: Foul Accumulation in the NBA
universal_lens: Bayesian gamma-distributed foul time modeling unifies player fatigue and strategic substitution across NBA match dynamics. Survival analysis of foul accumulation in NBA games using Gamma and Kaplan-Meier estimators to model time-to-foul-out distributions.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs conformal predictive inference on censoring constraints to estimate foul accumulation risk per player, enabling real-time tactical adjustments. Bayesian inference on foul-time predictive densities for player positioning and Q+1 guideline compliance using conformal prediction intervals.
gse_mapping: GSE encodes state transitions of player fouling using derived kernel operators to predict availability in late-game scenarios. Situational reasoning engine models coach decision trees for player substitution based on cumulative foul states and game context transitions.

primitives.name: Foul Time Distribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: A Bayesian analysis is presented based on the assumption that fouling times follow a Gamma distribution.

primitives.assumptions: Fouling times are independent and identically distributed according to a Gamma distribution with fixed parameters.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As n increases, the cumulative probability of nth foul approaches unity faster than linearly.

primitives.name: Nth Foul Acceleration
primitives.verbatim_quote: Various insights are obtained including the observation that players accumulate their nth foul more quickly for increasing n.
primitives.assumptions: Player fatigue increases monotonically with accumulated fouls, leading to faster subsequent foul rates.
